baseball_diamond: Baseball diamonds are characterized by a large green outfield and a brown dirt infield arranged in a diamond shape, unlike basketball courts which are flat rectangular surfaces with painted lines, unlike tennis courts which are smaller rectangular enclosures with nets, and unlike ground track fields which are continuous oval rings.
basketball_court: Basketball courts are rectangular paved areas with distinct painted line markings and hoops at each end, unlike baseball diamonds which have dirt infields and grass outfields, unlike tennis courts which are smaller rectangular enclosures, and unlike ground track fields which are large oval rings.
beach: Beaches are bright sandy strips directly adjacent to water bodies, unlike wetlands which have complex mixtures of water and vegetation, unlike islands which are landmasses surrounded by water, and unlike harbors which contain docks and moored ships.
bridge: Bridges are narrow linear elevated structures spanning water bodies or valleys, unlike overpasses which cross other roads over land, unlike railways which have continuous steel tracks on the ground, and unlike beaches which are sandy strips adjacent to water.
chaparral: Chaparral regions display dense irregular patches of low scrubby vegetation on hilly terrain, unlike forests which have tall dense tree canopies, unlike rectangular farmlands which are organized geometric plots, and unlike meadows which have uniform green grass textures.
church: Churches often appear as compact buildings with distinctive roofs, towers, or cross-like layouts, surrounded by small roads or open spaces, unlike commercial areas with dense large buildings, unlike palaces with large symmetrical courtyards, and unlike dense residential areas with tightly packed houses.
circular_farmland: Circular farmlands appear as large green or brown disks with center-pivot irrigation patterns, unlike rectangular farmlands which have straight geometric boundaries, unlike storage tanks which are small clustered circular structures, and unlike roundabouts which are small circular road junctions.
cloud: Clouds appear as bright white soft-edged regions with smooth or fluffy textures and weak ground structure, unlike snowbergs which are solid angular ice bodies, unlike sea ice which forms broken floe patterns, and unlike deserts which show continuous sandy textures.
commercial_area: Commercial areas consist of dense large-scale buildings with bright rooftops and adjacent parking lots, unlike parking lots which are flat asphalt surfaces with rows of cars, unlike dense residential areas which have smaller closely packed houses, and unlike industrial areas which feature large warehouses and storage yards.
dense_residential: Dense residential areas display tightly packed small houses with pitched roofs forming a continuous urban fabric, unlike sparse residential areas which have scattered isolated houses surrounded by vegetation, unlike commercial areas which have large flat-roofed buildings, and unlike rectangular farmlands which are organized geometric plots.
desert: Deserts show broad bare sandy or rocky surfaces with dry textures and little vegetation, unlike beaches which are adjacent to water, unlike mountains which have strong terrain relief and shadows, and unlike rectangular farmlands which show organized crop patterns.
forest: Forests are large expanses of dense dark green tree canopies with rough textures, unlike chaparral which has low scrubby vegetation, unlike rectangular farmlands which have organized geometric plots, and unlike mountains which have rugged rocky topography.
freeway: Freeways are wide continuous multi-lane roads with smooth asphalt, central dividers, and directional traffic flow, unlike overpasses which are elevated road structures spanning lower traffic, unlike intersections which are grid-like nodes where roads cross at-grade, and unlike railways which have continuous steel tracks.
golf_course: Golf courses contain broad managed green lawns, curved fairways, sand bunkers, and small water features, unlike meadows which are more uniform grasslands, unlike rectangular farmlands which have geometric crop plots, and unlike chaparral which has rough scrubby vegetation.
ground_track_field: Ground track fields feature large oval running tracks with a green infield, unlike baseball diamonds which have a dirt infield and grass outfield, unlike basketball courts which are small rectangular paved areas, and unlike tennis courts which are smaller rectangular enclosures.
harbor: Harbors are coastal facilities with dense linear piers, cranes, and moored ships, unlike beaches which are sandy strips, unlike bridges which are single elevated road crossings, and unlike industrial areas which have large warehouses without waterfront piers.
industrial_area: Industrial areas consist of large factory-like buildings, warehouses, storage yards, and sometimes tanks, unlike parking lots which are flat asphalt areas with rows of vehicles, unlike commercial areas which have denser building blocks, and unlike storage tanks which are mainly circular clustered structures.
intersection: Intersections are grid-like nodes where multiple roads cross at the same grade, unlike roundabouts which have circular central islands, unlike overpasses which are elevated structures separating traffic, and unlike freeways which are continuous multi-lane roads.
island: Islands are permanent landmasses with varied terrain completely surrounded by water, unlike ships which are distinct moving marine vessels, unlike sea ice which consists of broken irregular white floes, and unlike beaches which are sandy strips attached to the mainland.
lake: Lakes are large enclosed water bodies with smooth reflective surfaces, unlike rivers which are narrow winding channels, unlike wetlands which have complex mixtures of shallow water and vegetation, and unlike harbors which contain docks and ships.
meadow: Meadows are natural or semi-natural grasslands with uniform green textures, unlike rectangular farmlands which have organized geometric plots, unlike forests which have dense tree canopies, and unlike chaparral which has dense scrubby vegetation.
medium_residential: Medium residential areas display regularly arranged houses with moderate spacing and some open space, unlike dense residential areas which form continuous urban fabric, unlike sparse residential areas which have scattered houses, and unlike commercial areas which have larger buildings.
mobile_home_park: Mobile home parks contain rows of small narrow rectangular homes arranged in regular parallel patterns, unlike dense residential areas with varied rooftops, unlike parking lots with rows of vehicles, and unlike medium residential areas with larger houses and more open yards.
mountain: Mountains are large-scale elevated landforms with rugged topography, shaded slopes, and rocky textures, unlike forests which have dense tree canopies, unlike rectangular farmlands which are flat geometric plots, and unlike chaparral which has low scrubby vegetation on hills.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated linear road structures supported by pillars and casting shadows over lower intersecting traffic, unlike freeways which are ground-level continuous roads, unlike intersections which are ground-level crossing nodes, and unlike bridges which specifically span water bodies.
palace: Palaces often show large symmetrical building layouts, courtyards, formal gardens, and distinctive roof structures, unlike churches which are smaller with tower-like features, unlike commercial areas with dense functional buildings, and unlike medium residential areas with ordinary houses.
parking_lot: Parking lots are flat asphalt or paved areas with rows of parked cars and regular lane markings, unlike commercial areas which have dense large buildings, unlike airports which have long runways, and unlike industrial areas which contain large warehouses and storage yards.
railway: Railways are long linear tracks with parallel steel rails on gravel beds, unlike freeways which are wide paved multi-lane roads, unlike overpasses which are elevated road structures, and unlike railway stations which contain multiple tracks and platforms.
railway_station: Railway stations contain multiple parallel tracks, platforms, station buildings, and adjacent transport facilities, unlike railways which are mainly continuous linear tracks, unlike airports which have long runways, and unlike industrial areas which contain warehouses and storage yards.
rectangular_farmland: Rectangular farmlands consist of organized geometric plots with clear straight boundaries and varying crop textures, unlike forests which have dense tree canopies, unlike deserts which are bare sand expanses, and unlike meadows which are uniform grasslands without geometric boundaries.
river: Rivers are natural winding water channels with reflective surfaces and irregular banks, unlike lakes which are large enclosed water bodies, unlike bridges which are linear structures crossing water, and unlike harbors which contain docks and ships.
roundabout: Roundabouts feature a central circular island surrounded by a curved one-way traffic lane, unlike intersections which have perpendicular crossing roads, unlike circular farmlands which are much larger agricultural disks, and unlike freeways which are continuous multi-lane roads.
runway: Runways are extremely long wide paved strips with bright central lines and numeric markings, unlike freeways which are narrower with multiple lanes and central dividers, unlike parking lots which are grid-like car clusters, and unlike railways which have parallel steel tracks.
sea_ice: Sea ice appears as broken irregular white ice floes floating on dark ocean water, unlike islands which are permanent landmasses with varied terrain, unlike ships which are distinct elongated vessels, and unlike snowbergs which are large isolated glacial chunks.
ship: Ships are distinct elongated marine vessels navigating or moored in water, unlike airplanes which are cross-shaped objects on runways, unlike sea ice which consists of broken irregular white floes, and unlike islands which are permanent landmasses.
snowberg: Snowbergs are large isolated bright white glacial chunks floating in water, unlike sea ice which forms broken flat floes, unlike islands which are permanent landmasses with varied terrain, and unlike mountains which have rugged rocky shaded topography.
sparse_residential: Sparse residential areas display scattered isolated houses surrounded by vegetation or bare soil, unlike dense residential areas which form continuous urban fabric, unlike commercial areas which have large buildings, and unlike rectangular farmlands which are organized geometric plots.
stadium: Stadiums are large oval or rectangular enclosed structures with stands and central fields, unlike ground track fields which mainly show running tracks, unlike baseball diamonds which have diamond-shaped dirt infields, and unlike commercial areas which contain dense building blocks.
storage_tank: Storage tanks are circular white or metallic structures often clustered together, unlike industrial areas which have large rectangular buildings, unlike harbors which have docks and ships, and unlike circular farmlands which are much larger agricultural disks.
tennis_court: Tennis courts are small rectangular blue or green surfaced enclosures with central net lines, unlike basketball courts which have different painted court markings, unlike ground track fields which are large oval rings, and unlike baseball diamonds which have dirt infields.
terrace: Terraces appear as stepped contour-following agricultural strips on hillsides, unlike rectangular farmlands which are flat organized geometric plots, unlike mountains which have rugged continuous slopes, and unlike chaparral which has dense scrubby vegetation.
thermal_power_station: Thermal power stations feature large industrial buildings with tall chimney stacks and cooling towers, unlike industrial areas which have more general warehouses, unlike storage tanks which are circular metallic structures, and unlike commercial areas which have dense bright buildings.
wetland: Wetlands display complex mixtures of shallow water, mud, and patchy vegetation, unlike lakes which are smooth enclosed water bodies, unlike rivers which are winding water channels, and unlike forests which have dense tree canopies.
